RNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, June 24, 1924.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 16th instant with reference to the payment
by this Department of a grant toward the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School. I have noted for future
reference your opinion that the authority of the Governor in Council should be obtained before expenditures of this
nature are incurred.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 26, 1924.

SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 24th inst., replying to mine of the 16th with reference to a grant towards the
erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School.

In your reply you state that you have noted for future reference my opinion that the authority of the Governor in
Council should be obtained before expenditures of this nature are incurred.

While my previous letter did not so definitely state, still it was intended to express my opinion, not only that all future
payments of a like nature should be authorized by the Governor in Council, but all that such authority should be
obtained for the particular payment in question. I have accordingly to request that you take the necessary steps to
obtain the approval of the Governor in Council to this grant to St. Bruno's School.


Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

Indian Trust Fund: Refund of Payments made on Purchase of Land

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, October 12, 1925.

SIR. - In 1911 two quarter-sections on the Blackfoot Reserve were sold to Arthur M. Grace of Medicine Hat for
Krapfel and Grace under sales Nos. 242 and 243 for $4,080 and $4,140 respectively.

The terms of payment, apparently, were ten per cent on date of purchase and the balance in nine equal annual
payments, with interest at five per cent per annum on the unpaid balances.

Three annual payments were made on each contract but the interest, only, was paid in each case in the fourth year. On
principal account $1,224, was paid on sale No. 242 and $1,242 on sale No. 243, making a total of $2,466 on the two
sales.

No further payments were made, and these sales have been cancelled recently and the lots resold.

Cheque No. 1822 of the Indian Trust Fund, 1924 - 25, was issued Lorne M. Laidlaw, for an amount of $2,466, being in
full of the claim of Krapfel and Grace. This is the amount paid on the principal account under the sales contracts Nos.
242 and 243.

Please let me know the authority for the cancellation of these sales and the refund of the amounts paid thereon.

Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, October 14, 1925.

SIR, - I have before me your letter of the 12th instant, with reference to the above matter, and inquiring under what
authority these land sales were cancelled and refund made of the amounts paid thereon.

Cancellation of these sales was made under authority of section 61 of the Indian Act, and refund of amount of principal
paid thereon was made on order of the Superintendent General based on advice of the Department of Justice as set
forth in letter dated February 12, 1924.

I may say that this information has already been given to an employee of your Department.

Your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEan, Act. D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, November 11, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of October 14th with reference to the refund of payments made on
the purchase of Blackfoot Reserve Lands by Krapfel and Grace.

<!-- page 406 -->
You state that this refund was made on order of the Superintendent General based on advice of the Department of
Justice as set forth in letter dated February 12th, 1924.

I shall be obliged if you will send me a certified copy of the opinion of the Department of Justice to which you refer.

Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIR, November 13, 1925.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 11th instant, in the above matter, I enclose herewith certified copies of the
documents requested.


Your obedient servant,
D.C. SCOTT, Deputy Superintendent General.

The Asst. Auditor General.

OTTAWA, February 12, 1924.

SIR, - I have the honour to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of 2nd instant - 104A-1-17 - with respect to the sale
and cancellation of the W. 1/2 32-20-23, W.P.M., in the Blackfoot Reserve, in the Province of Alberta, in which you
request to be advised as to whether the cancellation was valid under the provisions of the Indian Act, and if so whether
the purchasers are entitled to any refund.

In reply I beg to state that the validity of the cancellation is not free from doubt as I am disposed to think that the
interested parties should have been given an opportunity to be heard and present their views, and any evidence, if any,
they may have had on their own behalf before the Superintendent General or the Deputy Superintendent General
decided to annul the sale. The fact that section 61 provides. that the Superintendent must be "satisfied" before he has
power to cancel seems to imply that he is required to hear all the parties before he proceeds to cancel the sale. In view
of the doubt as to the validity of the cancellation and the resale of the lands to another person, I would recommend that
your department make an effort to compromise the matter by refunding a portion of the purchase price paid by the
assignees or the whole of the amount if it be necessary to effect a settlement. My attention has been directed to an
opinion given by this department to your department in 1892 upon a similar provision in the Indian Act then in force
from which it appears that the writer of the opinion has no doubt that the cancellation could be made ex parte. I am not
prepared to adopt that opinion especially as the courts since the date of that opinion seem to lean more against the
forfeiture of rights acquired without giving parties interested an opportunity to be heard. I would recommend that in
future the department notify the parties interested of the

<!-- page 407 -->
intention of the department to cancel and give them an opportunity to be heard. The department should specify the time
and place of the hearing. The hearing can take place probably more conveniently in your department but in any case
ample time should be given prior to the hearing, and when a cancellation takes place those interested should be made
aware of it by notice or otherwise.

Papers, returned,
I have the honour to be, sir,
Your obedient servant,
E.L. NEWCOMBE.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

OTTAWA, December 18, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of 2nd instant - 104A-1-17 - upon the subject of the
cancellation of the sale of the W. 1/2 32-20-23 W. 4 M., in the Blackfoot Reserve, in the Province of Alberta. You
state that the amount of the purchase money, $2,466, paid to the Department, has been returned to the assignee who
now demands a further sum of $1,006.40, representing the interest on the sum referred to from, the dates of payments
to the date of cancellation. You wish to know whether this further sum now demanded could be legally taken from the
funds of the band and paid to the applicant, having regard to the provisions of sec. 61 of the Indian Act as enacted by
sec. 4, Chap. 47, 1924.

In reply I beg to state that the answer should be in the negative. It is, of course, as was pointed out in the letter from
this department oil the 12th February list, doubtful whether the cancellation of the sale made by the department was
effective, but the provisions of sec. 61, referred to, rendered the cancellation valid. The payment of the principal,
however, was made before the passing of the Act, which was assented to on the 19th July, 1924, and no exception can
therefore be taken to the refunding of the principal but the claim now for interest cannot be legally made.

YOURS truly,
W. STUART EDWARDS, D.M.J.

<!-- page 408 -->
Commission du Service civil : Traitement d'un inspecteur de construction

(Suite de la correspondance figurant à la page I - 225 du Rapport 1923 - 24)

BUREAU DE L'AUDITEUR GÉNÉRAL, 14 juillet 1925.

MONSIEUR, - Le 4 octobre 1924, l'Auditeur général vous a écrit au sujet du traitement attaché à la position
d'inspecteur de construction, demandant l'opinion de la, Commission quant à savoir si un inspecteur, employé plus ou
moins continuellement à traitement quotidien de $6 ou $7 par jour, pouvait recevoir jusqu'à $180 ou $210 par mois ou
si le montant payable dans un mois se limite au taux mensuel établi par la Commission.

Jusqu'ici, notre bureau n'a reçu aucune réponse à cette lettre, et comme la question dont il s'agit revient de temps à
autre, nous aimerions avoir une décision précise à ce sujet.

Je suis, monsieur, votre obéissant serviteur,
J.W. REID, pour l'A.G.
Le Secrétaire de la Commission du Service civil.
COMMISSION DU SERVICE CIVIL, le 23 juillet 1925.

CHER MONSIEUR, - On me prie d'accuser réception de votre lettre du 14 courant sur la question dont il est fait
mention ci-haut et de vous faire savoir qu'on vous avisera bientôt sur les points que vous avez soulevés.

Votre tout dévoué,
W. FORAN, secrétaire.

L'Auditeur général.

BUREAU DE L'AUDITEUR GÉNÉRAL, 12 octobre 1925.

MONSIEUR, - Le 4 octobre 1924 et le 14 juillet 1925, je vous ai écrit pour demander l'opinion de la Commission sur
la question de savoir si un inspecteur de construction employé à un traitement de $6 ou $7 par jour pouvait recevoir
jusqu'à $180 et $210 par mois, ou si la somme payable dans un mois est limitée par le taux mensuel établi.

Le 23 juillet 1925, vous avez répondu en disant que vous nous donneriez de nouveaux renseignements sous peu.

Je n'ai reçu aucune communication de votre part depuis. J'aimerais que vous m'envoyiez ces renseignements aussitôt
que possible.

Votre obéissant serviteur,
WM. KEARNS, A.G. adj.

Le Secrétaire de la Commission du Service civil.

NOTE DE L'A.G. - AU 31 décembre 1925, aucune réponse n'avait été recue à cette lettre.
